title: Every AI Company Is Accidentally Building a Bank — Dor Sasson, Stigg
talk_summary: A Stigg founder argues AI companies accidentally build banking-like financial infrastructure because token spend is checked after inference instead of before, causing overspend and concurrency bugs. He proposes synchronous pre-request entitlement/balance checks with async settlement, plus multi-source credit pools and per-agent budgets.

takeaways.what_they_do: Check entitlement and reserve budget synchronously at request time, then reconcile actual token usage asynchronously after the run completes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reserve before inference and settle actuals after

takeaways.what_they_do: Move the allow/deny decision for a request into the synchronous hot path rather than post-hoc logging, so spikes and overages are blocked before they happen.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hot path actually get checked synchronously, and everything that comes after uh is basically reconciled after

takeaways.technique: Multi-source credit pools with draw-down priority
takeaways.what_they_do: Track credits as separate pools by source (promotional, granted, paid) with a deterministic draw-down order instead of a single integer balance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each one of them is sourced from a different source. So, how do you decide which which one of them do you draw down against?

takeaways.what_they_do: Set budgets at the top of a hierarchy and enforce fine-grained caps per team, user, or agent, with visibility into who consumed what.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they demand different governance, different logics, allocations, budgets, spend caps

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat each consumption request as an idempotent, auditable transaction so retries and concurrent agents don't double-spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think about idempotency and auditability of those uh requests
